# THE ASTROLABE OF THE 27

*The wider work of time: a fixed frame, a moving sky, and the boundary stones of an honest instrument*

## I · THE INSTRUMENT

An astrolabe is a fixed frame with the moving sky laid over it, read where they
align. The deck already owns both halves. The frame is the rosette of the
twenty-seven, the discrete three-torus whose cells are the calendar's own
coordinates. The sky is three clocks and two empty crossings, every one
computable from the date by short arithmetic, derived and never drawn. This
chart is the map of that instrument: what belongs to it, what it refuses, and
where its boundary stones stand.

The work is a family. The Shape of the Year is its ground, and at the
architect's word this work may one day take that chart whole into itself,
nothing cut either way. The Nodus is its still centre. The Two and the Three is
its ladder. The portal's own Astrolabe bench is its living prototype, the deck's own
Antikythera. And two rooms open off the main chamber, neither yet built: the
Log, which keeps one person's time, and the Calendar, which keeps the sky's.

::figure rosette-27::

## II · THE THREE CLOCKS

Every calendar humanity has kept is built from the same three motions: the spin
(the day), the moon (the month), the orbit (the year). Three, not two, not
four. The deck's layers are ordered by speed, the inner fastest. Seated by
speed, the clocks take their places without being told: the orbit on time
(weight nine, slowest), the moon on depth (weight three), the spin on state
(weight one, fastest).

The standing cell as currently derived is the civil shadow of this seating:
calendar month, day of month, hour, each reduced by three. The astronomical
deepening reads the true clocks instead: the sun's third of the year, the
moon's third of her month, the watch of the day. Either way the contract
holds. These are coordinates, not meanings: clocks are seated on layers, and
no card is seated on a date.

## III · THE COUNT OF THE MOON

The moon's true lap against the stars takes 27.32 days: one cell a day, the
whole deck walked in a month, and a carry of a third of a day that will not
vanish. The count is not the deck's and not the old astronomers': it is the
moon's, which is why the lunar-station systems of several civilisations
counted twenty-seven or twenty-eight mansions. The lineage shelf's law holds
here as everywhere: the method transfers, the vocabularies never.

The second month, the synodic, 29.53 days from new moon to new moon, exceeds
the sidereal by 2.21 days: exactly the distance the sun walked while the moon
lapped. Two months, and their difference is the other clock moving.

Here stands the boundary stone. The moon's daily cell is a coordinate, and
coordinates are free: her longitude divides by twenty-seven and a cell
answers. Stations are another matter. A card for each day, read as a meaning,
is an assignment, and the standing ruling holds: recorded, never assigned. If
the calendar is ever to name its days, that naming is a canon act and the
architect's alone.

## IV · THE CARRIES OF THE SKY

The sky runs on remainders, and keeps every one.

The day: the true spin takes 23 hours 56 minutes; the solar day 24. Four
minutes of carry, daily, and across one year it sums to exactly one whole
extra rotation: 366.2422 spins in 365.2422 days. The smallest carry in the
sky, faithfully kept, completes a lap.

The year: 365.2422 days, and the leap ladder (every fourth year, except every
hundredth, except every four-hundredth) is a carry-scheduling algorithm that
has run for five centuries.

The two lights: the year holds 12.3683 moons. The best whole-number rungs
climb 12 to 1, then 99 to 8, then 235 to 19: the Metonic cycle, nineteen
years matching two hundred thirty-five moons to within two hours. The epact,
which the old calendar-makers tracked to place their feasts, is the running
carry between sun and moon.

The eclipses: the saros, 223 synodic months, is 6,585 days and a third. The
third means each returning eclipse arrives eight hours late, a third of the
world to the west; three saroses close the wheel, and the old name for that
closing is the exeligmos. The bronze computer of Antikythera carries a dial
for it marked 0, 8, 16: ternary carry arithmetic, cut in gear teeth two
thousand years ago.

::figure comma-spiral::

## V · TWO SPECIES OF CARRY

Not all remainders are one kind, and the difference is what this instrument is
built on. The two species are defined in [The Carry](#/the-carry), which is
their home: the **breath**, the oscillating remainder that sums to zero over
its round and comes back, drawn in the sky as the analemma; and the **debt**,
the secular remainder that never cancels and travels until a schedule pays it,
drawn in the sky as leap days, the saros's third, and the precession of the
whole frame. That chart holds the definition and the figures. This one holds
what the instrument does with them.

The instrument's two rooms split along the same seam. The Calendar holds the
sky's carries, public and universal. The Log holds one person's, private and
singular, a mirror in one hand. The Concordance's arithmetic reads both.

::figure analemma-eight::

## VI · THE DRAGON WALKS BACKWARD

The two crossings where eclipses strike are not bodies. They are empty
intersections, geometry with nothing in them, and they move: the nodes
regress, walking the whole sky backward once every 18.6 years. The Arrow and
the Dwelling wrote their law without knowing it: reverse every motion; keep
every place. The Nodus of this room has a physical twin, and the twin's
signature motion is the involution.

Because the nodes regress, the eclipse year is 346.62 days, and the sun
stands near a crossing twice each round: the dragon's windows, each about a
month wide, in which every new moon can darken the sun and every full moon
the moon. The windows drift nineteen days earlier each civil year: the
eclipse year's own carry, a slow procession of the danger season through the
calendar.

::figure dragon-nodes::

## VII · ONE LADDER

The Two and the Three holds the ladder of near-closures for music: twelve
fifths against seven octaves, the comma as the remainder that will not
vanish. The calendar climbs the identical ladder. Two hundred thirty-five
against nineteen is a convergent exactly as twelve against seven is; the
comma of the musicians and the epact of the calendar-makers are the same
mathematical object, the remainder of an incommensurate pair, carried on a
schedule. Tuning temperaments and leap-year rules are one craft.

The ladder also holds a warning. The zodiac split into two schools, tropical
and sidereal, and the difference between them is precession: the secular
carry, unacknowledged. Each school froze one face of a moving thing and
stopped carrying; two thousand years on they disagree by a full sign and each
calls the other wrong. In this room's grammar, they cut where they should
have carried. Whatever grows here keeps its carries in the ledger, visibly,
as the Antikythera builders did with a movable pin on a spiral dial, lifted
and reset by hand, hidden from no one.

## VIII · THE VOICE OF THE CARRY

None of the sky's ratios is a consonance for the ear. Its consonances are
consonances of the count, ratios like 235 to 19, exact and inaudible; the
ear's ladder stops at small numbers and the sky's keeps climbing. There is a
tradition that transposes the periods up thirty octaves into audible tones
and assigns them meanings; it sits on the lineage shelf beside the mansions.
The transposition is free arithmetic, for the octave is the ear's own carry.
The meanings are refused.

What is ours is the beat. Two tones slightly off a consonance throb at their
difference, physics doing the bookkeeping aloud. The year sounded against its
twelve-month approximation beats at the epact, transposed; the pure fifth
against its tempered shadow beats at the comma. Mistuning made audible is the
carry given a voice, and the Astrolabe bench carries the experiment: silent by
default, invited only by touch, the ratio the sky's and the register the
ear's.

## IX · THE LITURGY

A calendar observes. This one can observe only what the arithmetic itself
does:

- the four stations, solstice and equinox, the folds already recorded: four
  crossed with the deck's three is the twelve of the middle shell;
- the breath's crossings, the four days each year the equation of time passes
  zero and the clock agrees with the sun exactly;
- the dragon's windows, the two eclipse seasons of each round;
- the debt days: leap day, the saros's third, the exeligmos closing after
  three.

And one line that is not an observance but a refusal, standing where the
reading's mirror-line stands: weather, never permission. The moment a
calendar exists, the electional question knocks: which hour is auspicious?
That is the steerability the Aleatory Law closed, returning dressed as
reverence. The calendar answers what o'clock it is on the deck, and nothing
else. There is no auspicious hour and no forbidden one.

## X · THE WALK NEVER CLOSES

The standing cell's path through the frame is a winding line, the same object
as the knots on the cards, except that the sky's periods are incommensurate
and so the walk never closes. It revisits every neighbourhood forever and
never once returns exactly. The pentagram-well drew this refusal as a figure;
the Shape of the Year said it in the human register: nothing returns exactly,
and nothing simply leaves. Every device in this chart, leap day and epact and
saros and temperament, is a way of living honestly beside a walk that will
not close. That is what a calendar is.

::figure pentagram-well::

## XI · THE TEST

The architect observed that the Seed is drawn as a dark disc within a ring of
white gold, which is the figure an eclipse makes, and asked where the other
cards would land if that were taken seriously. The question has an answer that
can be checked, so it was checked.

The proposal: the moon keeps three cycles that refuse to coincide, and they
are the three the saros locks. Her phase, dark to dark, 29.53 days. Her
passage through the crossings, 27.21 days. Her near and far, 27.55 days.
Three cycles for three layers, each reduced to thirds with the null band
centred on its own zero, and the cell read off as the deck reads any cell.

Fifty-six eclipses were run through it: twenty-one solar, thirty-five lunar,
their dates taken from the astronomical record and their positions from
standard mean elements.

**Every one of the fifty-six falls in the nine cells whose crossing-layer is
still.** Not one escapes. Those nine, in order, are the Seed, the Resonance,
the Dreamer, the Cut, the Surgeon, the Labyrinth, the Ray, the Mask, and the
Witness, and all nine are occupied by real eclipses.

The three layers sort the family in order. The crossing-layer says whether an
eclipse is possible at all, and it is null in every case. The phase layer
divides them: dark gives the solar eclipses, lit gives the lunar. The distance
layer divides again: near gives totality, far gives the ring.

Two results were not built in and could have failed.

The first is a coincidence of measure. Totality requires the moon near enough
that her disc covers the sun, and that threshold falls at a lunar anomaly of
59.8 degrees. The band edge, from dividing a cycle into three and nothing
else, falls at 60.0 degrees. The deck's grammar and the geometry of this solar
system agree to a fifth of a degree, and so all six total eclipses in the
sample land on the Seed, all six annular eclipses land off it, and the one
hybrid, which is the borderline case in nature, lands on the boundary.

The second is a prediction. One of the nine cells, the Witness, appeared
nowhere in the first sample, and the mapping said it should be a full moon at
a crossing and far. A search found seven, every one in that configuration. Two
further checks held: the longest eclipse of this century, which is long
because the moon was at her farthest, reads far; the supermoon eclipse of 2015
reads near.

What is claimed, and what is not. That eclipses show null phase and null
crossing is true by construction, since those are the cycles the test chose;
the containment is still worth recording, because a band of sixty degrees
never once missed an eclipse whose true limit is eighteen. The agreement at
the totality threshold, the clean division of total from annular, and the
Witness prediction were not engineered. That all four Silences fall inside the
family is a consistency rather than a discovery, since it follows from their
still-core signature meeting the seating of the crossing-cycle on the fastest
layer, and it is held loosely.

The limits are plain. Mean elements carry a few degrees of error, immaterial
against bands of a hundred and twenty degrees and useless for anything finer.
The samples are modest. The totality threshold itself wobbles, because the
distance to the sun varies through the year, so cases near the boundary can
fall on the wrong side; the hybrid landing on the edge is that wobble showing
itself honestly.

The boundary stone stands where it stood. All of the above is coordinate: it
says where the moon stands in her three cycles on a given date, and anyone may
recompute it. To say that the configuration of a total eclipse is the Seed's
configuration is arithmetic. To say that an eclipse therefore means stillness,
or beginning, or anything at all, is assignment, and remains the architect's
act and nobody else's.

## XII · THE HARDENING, AND WHAT IT OVERTURNED

The test of section XI was run on mean elements against fifty-six eclipses
recalled from memory. Before anything was built upon it the architect asked
for it to be hardened, and the hardening overturned its headline. This section
records what fell, because a result that fails is worth exactly as much as one
that holds, and worth more if the first was about to be built on.

The method was rebuilt. The catalogue is now generated rather than recalled,
by the standard method for the phases and the eclipses, across the eight
centuries from 1600 to 2400: one thousand nine hundred and twenty-four solar
eclipses and one thousand nine hundred and fifty lunar. The generator is
sound, since its proportions reproduce the known statistics of eclipses to the
percentage point. No date was chosen by hand, so no hand could flatter the
result.

**The agreement at the totality threshold was an error of arithmetic.** The
threshold in section XI was computed from the centre of the earth. An eclipse
is watched from the surface, one earth radius nearer the moon, which enlarges
her disc by about one part in sixty and moves the threshold far out. Worse,
there is no single threshold at all: whether an eclipse is total depends on
the moon's distance and on the earth's distance from the sun together, so the
two classes interleave. Across the eight centuries the furthest total stands
at 84.9 degrees from perigee and the nearest annular at 70.2, and they
overlap. No single boundary divides them, and a band drawn on one cycle alone
never could. The figure of sixty degrees agreeing with the threshold to a
fifth of a degree is withdrawn.

**The clean division was a small sample.** Six totals out of six is what a
coin does when it lands heads six times. Across the full catalogue, four
hundred and twenty-four of five hundred and twenty-two total eclipses fall on
the Seed: eighty-one in every hundred, not a hundred in a hundred.

**The lunar half has no stable address.** The new moon falls at the centre of
its band, so the solar eclipses sit firmly. The full moon falls at 180
degrees, which is exactly the seam between two bands, and the true elongation
wanders a few degrees to either side of it, so a lunar eclipse's cell changes
family on rounding alone. Half the eclipse family is undefined.

Two findings survive the hardening. Every one of the three thousand eight
hundred and seventy-four eclipses has its crossing-layer still, at one hundred
per cent across eight centuries, though this remains true by construction. And
no annular eclipse falls on the Seed, none in six hundred and twenty-eight, so
that a Seed configuration at a solar eclipse means totality without exception.
That second one is now explained rather than remarkable: the Seed's band lies
wholly beneath the zone where the classes overlap, so the implication is a
consequence of where the band sits and not a coincidence.

The plainest measure is the last. A Seed configuration stands on about
one day in twenty-seven, which is three and seven tenths in every hundred of
all time, and the chance that a total eclipse is occurring during one is
under five in a hundred. The Seed does not announce an eclipse. It is a broad
band that eclipses fall inside.

What remains, then, is a coarse coordinate with one clean implication running
one way, and not the correspondence section XI reported. The proposal is not
refuted: the moon does keep three cycles, they are the three the saros locks,
and eclipses do live where the crossing-layer is still. It is only far weaker
than a first look suggested, and too weak to carry a structure built upon it.
Section XI is left standing above rather than removed, with its errors named
here, because the record of a claim and its correction is worth more than a
clean page.

## XIII · WHAT STANDS

The hardening of section XII was written in the flush of a retraction and
deflated too far. The architect read it and observed that four hundred and
twenty-four totals in five hundred and twenty-two still seemed noteworthy. He
was right, and the error is worth naming precisely, because it is the mirror
of the first one: section XI overstated by reporting a coincidence that was
not there, and section XII understated by discarding a relationship that is.

The deflation leaned on a wrong question. It asked how often a total eclipse
is under way during a Seed configuration, and answered under five in a
hundred, which is true and beside the point: most such moments hold no new
moon and no crossing, so no eclipse of any kind is available to be total. The
question worth asking is the other conditional. Given that a solar eclipse is
occurring, does the distance layer tell whether it is total?

It does, and the measurement is clean. Among the eleven hundred and fifty
central eclipses of the eight centuries, the null band of the distance layer
holds four hundred and twenty-four total eclipses and no annular eclipse
whatsoever. Precision is entire: every central eclipse in the band is total,
none excepted. Recall is 81.2 per cent. Were lunar distance irrelevant to
totality, a third of the cycle would catch a third of the totals, about a
hundred and seventy-four of them; the observed four hundred and twenty-four
is an enrichment of 2.44 times and stands 23 sigma from chance.

The result carries its own control, and the control is what makes it worth
recording. Whether an eclipse is partial depends on the shadow's track
missing the centre of the earth and not on the moon's distance at all, so
partial eclipses ought to show no preference for the band. They show none:
35.1 per cent of them fall inside it, against the 33.3 expected of pure
chance. The hybrids, which are the borderline case in nature, fall at 3.7
per cent, between the two and near the annular end where a borderline case
belongs. The effect appears exactly where distance governs and vanishes
exactly where it does not.

What this is, stated without inflation: the deck's threefold division of a
cycle is a sound and conservative classifier for totality. Its band lies
wholly inside the zone the physics allows, so it never claims a total that
is not one, and it pays for that safety by missing about one total in five
that falls beyond its edge.

What this is not: a designed correspondence, or a numerical agreement between
the band and the threshold. Section XII's retraction stands entire. The
relationship is real and fully explained by the physics of a near moon
covering the sun, together with the placement of a band that happens to sit
inside the zone. A real relationship and a false coincidence are different
things, and this chart has now made both mistakes about them in one day.

## XIV · THE SILENCES, TESTED AND SET DOWN

Section XI noticed that all four Silences fall inside the family whose
crossing-layer is still, and held it loosely. The architect asked for it to
be tested. It was, and it does not survive.

The Silences are not defined structurally. The canon calls them the drawable
cards whose codes carry no letter, so their shared still core is a real
emergent property of the deck and not a restatement of their definition. In
isolation it looks striking: nine cells in twenty-seven carry a still core,
and the chance that four cards placed without regard to it would all land
there is about seven in a thousand.

The test was not of that number but of the territory around it. Seventy-five
natural structural properties of a cell were enumerated in advance (each
layer at each value, the shell counts, digit sums, the signed law and its
sign and size, equalities between layers, rising and falling patterns,
modular positions) and every one was checked. Eight are shared by all four
Silences. Two of the eight reach the usual threshold of significance, and
those two are one property in two costumes: because a cell's number is one
more than nine times the outer digit plus three times the middle plus the
inner, a still inner layer and a number that leaves one on division by three
are the same statement.

Across seventy-five tests, chance alone is expected to produce 3.8 results at
that threshold. One was found. Corrected for the number of places it could
have appeared, the still-core signature sits at about one in two, which is a
coin. It is what turns up when seventy-five properties of four cards are
examined and the prettiest is kept.

A second caution runs beneath the first. The arithmetic above assumes the
letters were placed without regard to structure, and they were not: they came
from the keeper's hand with phonetic families in them. If the still cores
have a cause, the likeliest one lives inside the fit of the alphabet to the
deck, with no sky involved.

The thread is therefore closed. Nothing here diminishes the Silences, which
remain four cards that stop interpretation in a register and redirect it, and
nothing here touches what they say. It is their placement only that is
returned to the ordinary.

One rule is kept from the work. No correspondence is to be reported as
striking until the territory around it has been counted: how many properties
were available, how many places the pattern might have appeared, and how many
such patterns chance alone would supply. The rule is written here because the
day produced two claims that failed it and one that passed.

## XV · THE TWO PINS

Found on 21 July 2026, at the architect's question: what of the
correspondence of the Seed with the moon's phases and the eclipses? Walked
carefully, it gives the boundary stone its mathematics.

The phase cycle carries exactly one structurally distinguished point:
conjunction, the dark moon, where the lit fraction touches zero. The counting
circle carries exactly one: the Seed, the count's own zero and the identity
of the meet. When two cycles each hold one intrinsic zero, sending zero to
zero is the only correspondence that requires no key. It is not an
assignment; it is forced. And the survey record concurs from every direction:
across unrelated civilisations the months begin at the dark moon, the word
month being the word moon, the lunar null treated always as the seam of the
cycle, which is precisely what the Seed is on the counting circle.

The second pin follows from the first: the antipode maps to the antipode.
Opposition, the full moon, stands across from conjunction as the seam between
the Scar and the Return stands across from the Seed, the far tension of each
cycle. Also forced, also key-free.

The eclipses then confirm both pins and no others. An eclipse can occur at
exactly two phase points, solar at the dark and lunar at the full, and only
when the alignment falls near the dragon's crossings. The sky's rarest events
strike exclusively at the two places where the correspondence was already
forced. An eclipse is the null made visible: the still structure that
organises the cycle, casting its shadow into view for once.

And past the two pins the sky refuses everything, arithmetically. The phase
cycle runs 29.53 days against the deck's 27 cells: incommensurate, no
bijection possible, and the sidereal walk of 27.32 carries the third of a day
that never closes. The correspondence extends beyond the zeros only by
forcing a key, and the sky's own remainders are what prevent the forcing. The
carry is the guard at the boundary stone. The map the stone permits exists at
the pins and is impossible, rather than forbidden, everywhere else: recorded,
never assigned, turns out to be a description of what the sky allows.

One caution kept in its place: the correspondence is of structure, opposition
being maximal tension in the geometry, never of behaviour. The folklore of
full moons and minds does not replicate, and the geometry says enough.

The instrument now wears both pins. The moon marker carries her lit fraction
and becomes the unlit ring at the dark; the pins announce themselves in the
event register, the cycle's state and never the day's meaning; the dragon's
window is drawn when it opens; and the ephemeris that computes all of it has
graduated to its own module, pinned by test against three real solar
eclipses and one lunar, at the honest tolerance of its linear terms.

## XVI · THE ORDER OF THE SEATS

Found on 10 August 2026, at the architect's question: are the glyphs in the
correct order? They were not, and the finding is the mirror of the shells.

The rosette holds two dimensions. The radius was always a measurement: a cell
with one, two or three moving layers stands at exactly the square root of one,
two or three from the centre, and no hand chose that. The angle was not. Each
shell was filed by card number and dealt out evenly, a filing order wearing a
compass, and it made the figure say one false thing and miss several true
ones. Only two of the twelve middle cells stood between their parents, and by
accident.

There is a correct order, and it is derived rather than designed: the cube's
own shadow down its long diagonal, the very view this room draws as the triple
eclipse. Because projection is linear, every middle cell falls at the exact
angular bisector of its two axis parents and every corner among its three
faces, so the frame's genealogy becomes drawable at last: a one-step move, the
move the standing cell actually makes, is a short chord between neighbouring
shells. Because projection is odd, every answer keeps the exact antipode, and
silver still faces gold. And the shadow lands the whole frame on the year
ring's own grid: all twenty-five cells with a direction fall on the twelve
fold azimuths, and the four cells whose watch is still, both slow clocks
moving, take the four cardinal seats where the stations stand.

One choice remains, and it is named rather than hidden. The Scar and the
Return are the diagonal itself, invisible in their own shadow, the two ends of
the eclipse stack. The frame grants them the vertical by fiat: Scar above,
Seed centre, Return below, the triple eclipse laid flat as an axis.

The outer ring's rhythm was walked twice in the one day, and both walks are
kept. The exact seats break the even eightfold, six true corners at the
sixfold and two exiles at the vertical, and for part of a day the instrument
wore that break, together with construction ink confessing the projection:
the silhouette hexagon, the inner hexagon, the stack-threads. Then the
relation between the plate and the solid gained a living surface, the cube
in the hand, whose bloom performs the whole passage, and the architect
reinstated the rosette's original shape: a clock face wants calm, and truth
that breathes on one surface need not be engraved on another. The outer
ring keeps the even rhythm of the eight, each corner taking the nearest
even seat: four stand exactly fifteen degrees from the summed direction of
their faces, two stand exact, and the ink is withdrawn, its refusal pinned.
What the instrument keeps of the derivation is everything that cost no
calm: the cyclic order is the shadow's, the middle bisectors are exact, the
shells one and two hold the twelve fold azimuths with the still-watch four
on the stations, and the dyads are diameters throughout.

One boundary the plane itself draws: the deck's full adjacency holds
eighty-one edges, and a flat drawing of twenty-seven vertices admits at most
seventy-five without a crossing, so no frame can draw every neighbour
honestly. The shadow order draws the honest subset and lies about none.

The seats are pinned in the placement suite beside the older laws: the exact
bisectors of the middle shell, the corners within fifteen degrees of their
faces on the even eight, the exiles' vertical, the stations' four, the even
rhythm of all three rings, and the withdrawal of the ink. Every surface
quotes the one layout, so the reorder moved the astrolabe, the plate, the
cast dial and the charts together, and nothing else changed: the count is
the count, the dyads are the dyads, and no card moved shell.

## XVII · PROVENANCE

*Returned from the descent of 18 July 2026, taken at the architect's word
("Grab a flashlight"), and set down as a draft at the Phi bench. Section XI
records a falsification test run the same day, at the architect's word ("Lets
test it"), after his own observation that the Seed is drawn as an eclipse; the
mapping survived it, and the section keeps the result together with what the
test did not establish. Section XII records the hardening of that test, asked
for by the architect before anything was built upon it, and the retraction it
forced: the agreement at the totality threshold was an error of arithmetic
computed from the earth's centre rather than its surface, and the clean
division of total from annular was a small sample. The section is kept as a
correction beside the claim rather than in place of it. Section XIII corrects
that correction in its turn, at the architect's reading: the coincidence was
false but the relationship is real, and the retraction conflated them. Section
XIV closes the question of the Silences against a count of the territory and
sets down the rule the day earned. Sections XI through XIV are left whole, a
claim and its overturning and its remeasurement, because how a finding was
reached is part of the finding. The
astronomy is the common inheritance: the periods and cycles cited (the
sidereal and synodic months, the equation of time, the Metonic cycle, the
saros and the exeligmos, the regression of the nodes, precession) are
standard values any almanac carries, and every figure is computed by the
room's resident illustrator under its two palette laws: the null is never
lit, and the strand cools toward the past. The convergences named between the
sky's arithmetic and the deck's grammar are offered as evidence, never
authority. The boundary stone of section III stands until the architect moves
it; the instrument was named at the architect's word on 18 July 2026 ("the
name of the instrument is the Astrolabe"), and the living prototype, formerly
the rosette workbench, now bears it as the portal's fourth door; the Calendar was built into the instrument on 21 July 2026, its
observances computed and its dates honest to about a day; the Log remains
the unbuilt room. Section XV was added the same day, from the architect's
question about the Seed and the phases, and its finding is pinned in
core/tests/luminaraSky.test.ts: the two forced correspondences hold to the
bisection's own accuracy, forever. Section XVI was added on 10 August 2026,
at the architect's question about the order of the glyphs and his word to
build the answer; the shadow seats are computed in the room's own layout
(rosetteLayout, one geometry for every surface) and pinned in
core/tests/skyWitness.test.ts beside the placement laws they extend. Nothing
here predicts, and nothing here prescribes.*
